Saving an empty or nonempty launch script changes configuration without executing it.
Manual launch must bind workspace, terminal and ready generation before one stdin write.
A setup restart failure must not be mistaken for successful restart or script completion.
A setup marker existence decision must remain distinct from an execution receipt.
Persist marker provenance and reject equating mark-ran with successful exit.
Open an existing stale PTY registry entry and observe liveness and resource cleanup separately.
Closed-stream write cleanup must not remove a replacement generation; flush is not command success.
Resize visible sessions and enforce minimum geometry without opening another PTY.
Injected PTY kill failure must remain visible after registry removal; no all-stopped receipt.
PTY read EOF and read error must not impersonate child exit status.
Two concurrent opens must account for both spawned candidates and failed compensation.
Fail after worktree creation and before session/config persistence; preserve partial disk effects.
Remove worktree with missing parent or prune error; distinguish stopped process from deleted disk.
Copy AGENTS through temporary file; exercise copy and rename cleanup failures without authorizing scripts.
Apply a conflicting patch into the parent repository and expose partial application.
Stage renamed paths; second-path failure must preserve the first-path result.
Stage-all is an index mutation, not a status query.
Unstage rename pairs without discarding unrelated working-tree changes.
Exercise every restore failure leading to clean; do not assume only missing files trigger fallback.
Keep revert-all confirmation and expose restore-success/clean-failure partial loss.
Commit invokes external hooks and credentials under a captured program/env/cwd boundary.
A failed pre-push fetch does not erase the subsequent push attempt or remote result.
Replay pull fallback parameter branches with independent repository-state assertions.
Fetch/prune changes local refs even when treated as a remote read.
Pull success followed by push failure must not trigger blind replay of the whole sync.
Initialization may succeed while initial commit fails; preserve confirmation and partial status.
Account separately for repo creation, origin, push and default-branch PATCH.
PR checkout is a local mutation and network-capable operation, not PR preview.
Issue total fallback to returned-list length must be labelled incomplete.
PR total fallback must not claim all remote PRs were enumerated.
Parse quoted and renamed PR diff paths without extending the authorized root.
Issue-comments endpoint and first-page output must not be labelled all review comments.
Libgit2 branch enumeration remains represented without a Command constructor.
Safe checkout and HEAD update are separately checked for failure.
Branch creation surviving a failed checkout must remain visible.
Startup ready signaling must bind installer receipt and actual product readiness.
Auto-check guards and previous-failure consumption must be tested separately.
Native updater menu must reach check/download rather than a UI-only state change.
Failed install after pending-version storage must preserve truthful pending state.
Release-notes fetch remains a separate network entry when auto-check is disabled.
Pending-version storage failure must not become installation authority.
Icon sync deletes then copies; missing dependency and failed copy have distinct outcomes.
Doctor installation advice is not an executable installer edge.
Tauri icon generation is a pinned external build writer, not a pure script string.
Desktop path filters and pre-smoke artifacts do not prove all PR CI or runtime verification.
No-Publish mode still accesses signing material and writes artifacts.
Release-view authorization/network failure must not be classified as confirmed nonexistence.
Manifest rewrite and signature write are two effects with version rejection checks.
NewKey protection of private key does not imply protection of existing public-key output.
Installer smoke is a real install/uninstall/process test and requires separate authorization.
Local mode with an existing daemon must not bypass the remote-sealing startup policy.
Application exit after ignored daemon-stop failure cannot assert descendants stopped.
Restart closes state first and does not itself create the replacement PTY.
Remote adapter errors must not silently fall through to a second local execution.
